related_questions.question: What are the new quarantine requirements for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Updated Guidance: The updated Respiratory Virus Guidance recommends that people stay home and away from others until at least 24 hours after both their symptoms are getting better overall, and they have not had a fever (and are not using fever-reducing medication).
related_questions.title: Respiratory Virus Guidance Update Frequently Asked Questions - CDC

related_questions.question: What are the isolation rules in NSW for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: There are currently no rules in NSW which require you to self-isolate if you test positive to COVID-19, but it is strongly recommended you stay home until your symptoms have gone and take steps to protect others. Most people with COVID-19 can manage safely at home.
related_questions.title: Testing positive to COVID-19 and managing COVID-19 safely at home

related_questions.question: What is the COVID risk management plan?
related_questions.snippet: The aim of a COVID-19 Risk Management Plan for organisations is to identify points of contact (risks) between your employees and the people of the designated area during delivery of the 'essential activity' and to put in place appropriate controls to minimise this exposure.
related_questions.title: Organisations COVID-19 Risk Management Plan – Essential Activity

related_questions.question: What are the rules for COVID positive in NSW?
related_questions.title: If you test positive for COVID-19 you should:
list: stay at home until your symptoms are gone.
monitor your symptoms – if your symptoms worsen, see your doctor.
see your doctor for oral treatments if you are in a high-risk group.
follow the advice of your state or territory health agency.
